title: Everyday Health
description: Look after your body with the basics: nutrition, sleep, movement, and light first aid.

stations.title: Balanced Nutrition
stations.summary: There is no magic food. What works is the pattern you repeat every single day.
points: The healthy plate: half vegetables & fruit, a quarter carbohydrates, a quarter protein.
Choose fibre-rich carbohydrates (brown rice, sweet potato, wholegrain bread) over refined ones.
Limit sugar, salt, and excess oil — controlled, not eliminated.
Drink enough water; thirst is a late signal.

questions.prompt: According to the healthy plate guide, the recommended split is...
options: ½ carbohydrates, ¼ vegetables, ¼ protein
½ vegetables & fruit, ¼ carbohydrates, ¼ protein
questions.explain: Half the plate is vegetables and fruit; the rest is split between carbohydrates and protein.

options: Sipping small amounts throughout the day
Drinking 2 litres at once before bed
Replacing all water with sweet drinks
questions.explain: Regular sips beat waiting for thirst. Needs vary with activity, weather, and body condition.

questions.prompt: Long-term excess salt intake is most often linked to...
questions.explain: Excess sodium makes the body retain fluid and raises blood pressure — a key risk for heart disease and stroke.

cards.back: ½ vegetables & fruit · ¼ carbohydrates · ¼ protein

stations.title: Quality Sleep
stations.summary: Sleep is not wasted time — that is when body and brain do their repairs.
points: General needs: adults 7–9 hours, teenagers 8–10 hours a night.
A consistent sleep-wake schedule often matters more than an occasional long night.
Cut caffeine in the afternoon/evening and keep bright screens away before bed.
A short ritual (dim lights, light stretching) helps the brain switch to rest mode.

questions.prompt: The usual sleep need for an adult is...
questions.explain: Most adults need 7–9 hours. Teenagers need more, around 8–10 hours.

questions.prompt: The most immediate effect of too little sleep is...
questions.explain: Sleep loss lowers concentration, shortens your fuse, and weakens immunity.

questions.prompt: Which habit best supports sleep quality?
options: Scrolling on your phone in bed until you drop
questions.explain: Circadian rhythm loves regularity. A stable wake time teaches the body when to sleep.

cards.back: A consistent schedule, not rare long nights

stations.title: Physical Activity
stations.summary: A little movement every day beats a lot of movement once in a while.
points: General guideline: at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week (e.g. brisk walking 30 min × 5 days).
Add strength training twice a week to protect muscles and bones.
Stretch lightly every 30–60 minutes when you must sit for long periods.
Take the stairs, get off one stop earlier — small consistent movement still counts.

questions.prompt: The recommended minimum physical activity for adults is...
options: 150 minutes of moderate intensity per week
60 minutes daily with no rest days
questions.explain: The common WHO figure is 150 minutes moderate or 75 minutes vigorous per week.

questions.prompt: If your job requires long hours of sitting, the wisest habit is...
options: Stand and stretch lightly every 30–60 minutes
Hold your breath for a few seconds
questions.explain: Prolonged sitting slows circulation. Short movement breaks help muscles and focus.

questions.prompt: The most accurate benefit of regular physical activity is...
options: It lowers heart disease risk and improves mood
It replaces the need for sleep
It means you no longer need vegetables
questions.explain: Regular exercise protects the heart, blood sugar, and weight, and supports mental health.

cards.back: ≥150 minutes moderate (e.g. brisk walk 30 min × 5 days)
Break it with standing/stretching every 30–60 min

stations.title: Basic First Aid
stations.summary: For emergencies, call emergency services first. For minor injuries, use the right steps.
points: Grazes: rinse with running water and soap, dry, then cover with a clean dressing.
Minor burns: run clean (not ice) water over it for 10–20 minutes; never apply toothpaste, soy sauce, or butter.
Nosebleeds: sit up, lean slightly forward, pinch the soft part of the nose for about 10 minutes; do not tilt the head back.
Seek medical care immediately for: deep or wide wounds, bleeding that will not stop, breathlessness, reduced consciousness, or fever lasting more than 3 days.

questions.prompt: Correct first treatment for a minor burn is...
options: Spread toothpaste or butter on it
Run clean water over it for 10–20 minutes
Press ice cubes directly onto it
questions.explain: Running water cools the tissue. Ice and toothpaste can worsen the burn and raise infection risk.

questions.prompt: During a nosebleed, the correct position is...
options: Sitting up and leaning slightly forward
Tilting the head as far back as possible
Bending down with your head below your knees
questions.explain: Leaning forward stops blood running down the throat. Tilting back makes you swallow it.

questions.prompt: Which sign needs immediate medical care?
options: A small graze on a finger
questions.explain: Breathlessness, uncontrolled bleeding, and reduced consciousness are emergencies — do not wait.

cards.back: Running water 10–20 min (no ice, no toothpaste)
Sit, lean forward, pinch the nose ~10 min
